data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Crash-only software with resurrection logs: safety is achieved by never distinguishing between crash and restart; the durable record is a birth certificate that enables idempotent workspace reconstruction rather than hazardous reclamation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Deterministic replay must be total; any external I/O or nondeterminism invalidates the guarantee","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Log replay cost may be prohibitive for large workspaces","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Requires the workspace storage to be content-addressed or journaled to avoid corruption between incarnations","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"On every startup, the process writes a birth certificate (problem_id, deterministic_seed, workspace_path, incarnation_number) to durable storage. All writes to the workspace are idempotent and logged in a redo log. 'Reclamation' is simply a new process incarnation reading the birth certificate and replaying the log to determine if evidence was already completed. If completed, the workspace is re-adopted; if not, it is reconstructed. The causal mechanism is deterministic replay: the workspace is not a resource to reclaim but a function of the durable birth certificate and log. This protocol never displaces evidence because there is no separate reclamation step\u2014only continuation. Adjudication: this dominates both log and lease protocols when determinism holds, by eliminating the orphan-detection problem entirely.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
